question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III AIF, CTA / managed-futures style) wishes to select a global peer benchmark for its PPM. Which of the following is the MOST widely-used hedge-fund index family produced by Hedge Fund Research, Inc. and structured by strategy (e.g., Macro, Equity Hedge, Event-Driven, Relative Value)?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** HFRI (Hedge Fund Research Inc.) publishes strategy-tiered sub-indices — HFRI Macro, HFRI Equity Hedge, HFRI Event-Driven, HFRI Relative Value, HFRI Fund Weighted Composite — that are the industry-standard peer benchmarks for hedge funds globally. Credit Suisse/Tremont, Eurekahedge, and Barclay Hedge are alternatives. MSCI World, S&P Global BMI, and FTSE bond indices are EQUITY / BOND market indices, not hedge-fund peer indices. **The Trap:** Options B (MSCI World GDP), C (S&P Global BMI), and D (FTSE Russell Govt Bond) are legitimate broad-market indices covered in the chapter, but none is a hedge-fund peer index. HFRI is the standard answer for hedge-fund peer benchmarking. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B / XIX-C also test hedge-fund index names. HFRI is referenced across all Cat III content; it is NOT used for Cat I/II AIFs (those use PE/VC vintages from Cambridge/Preqin). **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For an Indian Cat III CTA fund's PPM, disclose the HFRI Macro / CTA sub-index alongside the CRISIL AIF Cat III index. LPs want BOTH — a domestic peer (CRISIL) and a global strategy peer (HFRI) — because your strategy's natural peer set is typically global managed-futures managers, not Indian long-only funds.
